title: Professional SQL & Databases Official QBank - Section 2

questions.question: Which statement best describes a relational database?

options.text: Data is stored as independent files without defined relationships.
Data is arranged as a tree where each record has one parent.
Data is organized into related tables made of rows and columns.
Data is kept as flexible documents with semi-structured fields.

questions.question: What is the main role of a PRIMARY KEY?

options.text: It uniquely identifies each row in a table.
It automatically connects every table in a database.
It stores repeated values used for grouping rows.
It converts text values into numeric identifiers.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of an ER diagram in database design?

options.text: To represent entities, attributes, and relationships visually.
To execute data updates before creating database tables.
To assign permissions to users and database roles.
To calculate aggregate values across related tables.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a weak entity?

options.text: It is an independent entity with its own complete key.
It is an entity that contains only multivalued attributes.
It depends on a strong parent entity for its existence.
It is an entity used only as a data warehouse fact table.

questions.question: When mapping a 1:N relationship, where is the foreign key usually placed?

options.text: The key from the N side is added to the 1 side.
The key from the 1 side is added to the N side.
A junction table is created between the two entities.
No foreign key is needed when cardinality is 1:N.

questions.question: How is an M:N relationship usually mapped to relational tables?

options.text: Merge both entities into one table with repeated columns.
Place the first entity key only inside the second table.
Place the second entity key only inside the first table.
Create a junction table containing keys from both entities.

questions.question:
What value is returned by the following query?
SELECT 8 + 4 * 2 AS Result;
Which statement correctly compares star and snowflake schemas?

options.text: Star normalizes dimensions heavily; snowflake keeps dimensions flat.
Star uses no fact table; snowflake uses one fact table with no dimensions.
Star and snowflake use the same dimension structure and join complexity.
Star uses flatter dimensions; snowflake uses more normalized sub-dimensions.

questions.question: Which data type is most suitable for storing a value such as 1250.75 exactly?

options.text: INT, which stores whole numeric values
VARCHAR(20), which stores variable text
DECIMAL(10,2), which stores fixed-point values
DATE, which stores calendar date values

questions.question: Which constraint is most appropriate for enforcing Price > 0?

options.text: PRIMARY KEY
CHECK
UNIQUE
NOT NULL

questions.question: Which DDL statement is used to modify the structure of an existing table?

options.text: INSERT INTO
UPDATE
SELECT
ALTER TABLE

questions.question:
Which DDL command removes all rows, frees the table space, and keeps the table
structure?

options.text: DELETE FROM table_name
DROP TABLE table_name
ALTER TABLE table_name
TRUNCATE TABLE table_name

questions.question: Which SQL statement is used to add a new row to a table?

options.text: INSERT INTO
UPDATE
DELETE FROM
SELECT

questions.question: Which command is used to give a user database privileges?

options.text: REVOKE
GRANT
COMMIT
SAVEPOINT

questions.question:
The Students table contains (Ahmed, 55), (Mona, 80), and (Ali, 65). What value is
returned by the following query?
SELECT COUNT(*) AS StudentCount
FROM Students
WHERE Score >= 60;

The Orders table contains (Cairo, 300), (Cairo, 250), (Giza, 600), and (Alex, 400). Which
cities are returned by the following query?
SELECT City, SUM(Amount) AS TotalAmount
FROM Orders
GROUP BY City
HAVING SUM(Amount) >= 550;

options.text: Cairo only
Giza only
Cairo and Alex
Cairo and Giza

questions.question: Which query returns the names and ages of customers whose age is greater than 30?

options.text: SELECT name, age FROM customers WHERE age >= 30;
SELECT name, age FROM customers WHERE age = 30;
SELECT name, age FROM customers WHERE age > 30;
SELECT name, age FROM customers WHERE age BETWEEN 0 AND 30;

questions.question:
Which ORDER BY clause sorts older customers first and, for equal ages, sorts names
alphabetically?

options.text: ORDER BY age DESC, name ASC;
ORDER BY age ASC, name DESC;
ORDER BY age DESC, name DESC;
ORDER BY age ASC, name ASC;

questions.question: What is the purpose of DISTINCT in a SELECT query?

options.text: It sorts the returned rows by one or more columns.
It groups rows before an aggregate function is applied.
It removes duplicate rows or values from the result.
It filters rows whose selected columns contain NULL.

questions.question: Which query correctly counts the number of customers in each city?

options.text: SELECT city, COUNT(*) FROM customers;
SELECT city, COUNT(*) FROM customers GROUP BY city;
SELECT city, COUNT(*) FROM customers GROUP BY customer_id;
SELECT DISTINCT city, customer_id FROM customers;

questions.question:
A Customers table has 10 rows, and Phone is NULL in 2 rows. What does SELECT
COUNT(*), COUNT(Phone) return?

options.text: 8 and 8
10 and 8
8 and 10
10 and 10

questions.question: Which condition correctly returns rows where Phone has a missing value?

options.text: WHERE Phone IS NULL
WHERE Phone = NULL
WHERE Phone IN NULL
WHERE Phone LIKE NULL

questions.question: How does BETWEEN 20 AND 35 treat its boundary values in SQL?

options.text: Both 20 and 35 are included in the range.
Both 20 and 35 are excluded from the range.
20 is included while 35 is excluded from the range.
20 is excluded while 35 is included in the range.

questions.question: Which condition returns names that start with the letter A?

options.text: WHERE Name LIKE '%A'
WHERE Name LIKE '%A%'
WHERE Name LIKE 'A%'
WHERE Name LIKE '_A%'

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares WHERE and HAVING?

options.text: WHERE filters groups; HAVING sorts the grouped result.
WHERE sorts rows; HAVING removes duplicate group values.
WHERE filters rows; HAVING filters grouped or aggregated results.
WHERE creates groups; HAVING filters rows before grouping occurs.

questions.question: Which query finds email values that occur more than once?

options.text: SELECT Email, COUNT(*) FROM Customers GROUP BY Email HAVING COUNT(*) = 1;
SELECT Email, COUNT(*) FROM Customers GROUP BY Email HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1;
SELECT Email, COUNT(*) FROM Customers GROUP BY Email HAVING COUNT(*) < 1;
SELECT Email, COUNT(*) FROM Customers GROUP BY Email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

questions.question: Which expression displays 'NO PHONE' when Phone is NULL?

options.text: NULLIF(Phone, 'NO PHONE')
COALESCE(Phone, 'NO PHONE')
CONCAT(Phone, 'NO PHONE')
SUBSTRING(Phone, 'NO PHONE')

questions.question:
What is the output category for Age = 42 in the following logic?
CASE
WHEN Age < 25 THEN 'Young'
WHEN Age BETWEEN 25 AND 40 THEN 'Adult'
ELSE 'Senior'
END

options.text: Young
Adult
NULL
Senior

questions.question:
Which expression adds 7 days to OrderDate using the date syntax taught in Session
5?

options.text: DATE_ADD(OrderDate, INTERVAL 7 DAY)
DATE_ADD(OrderDate, INTERVAL 7 MONTH)
DATEDIFF(OrderDate, INTERVAL 7 DAY)
DATE_ADD(7, INTERVAL OrderDate DAY)

questions.question:
In SQL Server, which construct chooses between two statement blocks based on a
Boolean condition?

options.text: CASE expression
PIVOT operator
WITH clause
IF...ELSE statement

questions.question: What is the main risk of running an UPDATE statement without a WHERE clause?

options.text: All rows in the table may be updated.
Only the first matching row may be updated.
The statement automatically becomes a SELECT.
No row can be changed without a WHERE clause.

questions.question: What does an INNER JOIN return?

options.text: All rows from the left table regardless of matching rows.
All rows from both tables including every unmatched row.
Rows that have matching join values in both tables.
Every possible combination of rows from both tables.

questions.question: What does a LEFT JOIN return?

options.text: Only rows that have a match in both joined tables.
All rows from the right table plus matches from the left.
Only rows from the left table that have no right-side match.
All rows from the left table plus matching rows from the right.

questions.question: Which situation is a typical use of a SELF JOIN?

options.text: Matching employees to supervisors stored in the same table.
Combining current employees with retired employees using UNION.
Connecting orders to customers using a foreign key relationship.
Grouping product rows by category before calculating totals.

questions.question:
Customers contains (1, Ahmed), (2, Mona), and (3, Salma). Orders contains (101, 1),
(102, 1), and (103, 2). Which result is returned by the following query?
SELECT c.CustomerName, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS OrderCount
FROM Customers c
LEFT JOIN Orders o
ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.CustomerName
ORDER BY c.CustomerID;

options.text: Ahmed: 2, Mona: 1
Ahmed: 2, Mona: 1, Salma: 0
Ahmed: 1, Mona: 1, Salma: 1
Ahmed: 2, Mona: 1, Salma: 1

questions.question: For a regular non-correlated subquery, what is generally evaluated first?

options.text: The inner query is evaluated before the outer query uses its result.
The outer query is completed before the inner query is evaluated.
The GROUP BY clause is evaluated before either SELECT statement.
Both queries must always be evaluated at exactly the same time.

questions.question:
The Employees table contains (Ahmed, 4000), (Mona, 6000), and (Salma, 8000). Which
employee is returned by the following query?
SELECT EmployeeName
FROM Employees
WHERE Salary > (
SELECT AVG(Salary)
FROM Employees
);

options.text: Ahmed
Salma
Mona
Mona and Salma

questions.question:
What does this condition require?
Price > ALL (SELECT Price FROM Products WHERE Category = 'Budget')

options.text: Price must be greater than at least one returned price.
Price must be equal to the largest returned price.
Price must be greater than the average returned price.
Price must be greater than every returned price.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of EXISTS in a WHERE condition?

options.text: To return the number of rows produced by a subquery.
To return a single scalar value from a subquery.
To test whether the subquery returns at least one row.
To sort the rows returned by a nested SELECT statement.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares UNION and UNION ALL?

options.text: UNION keeps duplicates, while UNION ALL removes duplicates.
UNION removes duplicate rows, while UNION ALL keeps them.
UNION sorts columns, while UNION ALL groups matching columns.
UNION joins tables by keys, while UNION ALL creates a subquery.

questions.question:
What is a key difference between a window function and a GROUP BY aggregate
query?

options.text: A window function can be used only with text columns.
A window function removes row-level detail before calculating.
A window function requires a permanent temporary table first.
A window function can calculate across rows while retaining row detail.

questions.question:
Salaries are 9000, 9000, and 8000 in descending order. What ranks are produced by
RANK()?

Salaries are 9000, 9000, and 8000 in descending order. What ranks are produced by
DENSE_RANK()?
Which statement about ROW_NUMBER() is correct?

options.text: It assigns a unique sequential number to each row in the ordered result.
It gives tied rows the same number and skips the next rank.
It gives tied rows the same number without creating rank gaps.
It returns a value from the row immediately before the current row.

questions.question: Which window function returns a value from the row that precedes the current row?

options.text: LEAD()
RANK()
AVG() OVER()
LAG()

questions.question:
In the query WITH HighEarners AS (...) SELECT ... FROM HighEarners, what is
HighEarners?

options.text: A temporary named result set available to the main query.
A permanent table created automatically in the database.
A stored procedure that executes before the SELECT statement.
A database view that remains available after the query ends.

questions.question: What is the main transformation performed by PIVOT?

options.text: It converts multiple columns into separate database tables.
It turns unique row values into columns using an aggregation.
It replaces NULL values with default values before grouping.
It joins a fact table to all related dimension tables.

questions.question: What happens when a runtime error occurs inside a BEGIN TRY block in SQL Server?

options.text: The transaction is committed before the error is reported.
The query continues directly with the next statement in TRY.
Execution moves to the associated BEGIN CATCH block.
The statement is converted into an IF...ELSE condition.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a database view?

options.text: A physical copy of table data stored as a second base table.
A virtual table whose result is defined by a stored query.
A transaction marker used to support a partial rollback.
A permission rule that grants access to selected columns.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a stored procedure?

options.text: A virtual result set that behaves like a query-based table.
A named stored set of SQL statements that can be executed and reused.
A constraint that checks new rows before they are inserted.
A temporary result created by a WITH clause for one query.
